newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends mixed, PV finishes higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends mixed, PV finishes higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended mixed Friday with Palo Verde (PV) futures finishing higher on concerns over nuclear power unit outages in the U.S. West, industry sources said.
"The unit outages affected the cash market and affected March (PV) and dragged April along with it," said one futures trader.
March PV ended up 28 cents at $13.82 per megawatt hour (MWh) after trade in a range of $13.55-14.15, while April PV ended up 30 cents at $12.85 from trade in a range of $12.70-13.00 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds settled between 10 cents lower and 30 cents higher.
March California Oregon Border (COB) closed down 17 cents at $10.30 after exchanges in a range of $10.20-10.40, while April COB settled unchanged at $9.95 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds finished between 20 cents lower and five cents higher.
Upward pressure was seen on PV futures from an extended outage at Southern California Edison's 1,070 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant in southern California.
A maintenance and refueling outage at the unit has been extended into early March. The unit was shut November 30, 1996.

With the extension, the outage will overlap with a planned maintenance and refueling outage at Arizona Public's 1,221 MW Palo Verde unit 3 in Arizona set to begin Feb 22 and last an estimated 50 days.

But traders stated any impact from the Western nuclear outages was expected to be short term, with continued downward pressure expected over the longer term from forecasts of above average spring hydroelectric production.
Also, southbound flows on the AC Pacific Intertie between the Northwest and California were expected to be reduced to 2,800 MW from 3,200 MW on March 1 and 2 for maintenance.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were forecast to average five to 10 degrees above normal through Tuesday with little or no precipitation.
In the Southwest, temperatures six to 12 degrees above normal were expected to last into early next week with little or no precipitation.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 145 COB and 213 PV contracts traded Friday.
